answers.answer: Build the 10-card deck with all 4 Conflict III cards on the bottom, 5 of 9 Conflict II cards above them, and 1 of 3 Conflict I cards on top; return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: “1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom”; unused cards return “without looking.”

answers.answer: Four-player human: start at 1 VP; three-player human: start at 0 VP. Each starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 3 troops in the nearby garrison and 9 in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; “two Agents” and third Agent as Swordmaster; 3 troops and remaining 9; take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may Reveal while Agents remain; after Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards still in hand and revealed on the Reveal turn, not Agent-turn cards. On Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Reveal Turn: “Agent turns are optional”; after Reveal “turns are skipped”; resolve “just-revealed cards only”; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue played before Agent placement may grant resources that pay the entry cost. Resources gained after placement from the destination or Agent card cannot pay that entry cost. One card chooses only one Agent icon and cannot send multiple Agents; a card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot can precede placement and its prior gains pay entry; post-placement gains cannot. Agent Turn: “You choose only one Agent icon”; no Agent icons means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison, for up to 5. At a non-Combat space, the recruited troops stay in the garrison. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: cube recruits from supply to garrison; at Combat spaces deploy any/all recruited this turn plus “up to two more” from garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where your Spy is; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent at that space, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing an Agent to draw a card; decide immediately after placement and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay both; different Spies may pay Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent “do not recall”; Infiltrate bypasses another’s Agent only; Gather Intelligence timing is immediately after placement; cannot recall same Spy for both, but different Spies may be used.

answers.answer: Two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4, for 11 strength. If your final Conflict unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in Combat Intrigue without a unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; last unit removed means 0. Combat phase: only players with “at least one unit” may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes, you may act again after an opponent plays; a prior pass does not bind you. The window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops go to supply and sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; closes after consecutive passes. Resolve Combat: troops return to supply and sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: Four players tied for first each take the second reward; if exactly two tied, remaining players compete for third. Three players tied for first each take second reward and no other rewards are given. In either tie-for-first case nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Combat ties table: first tie with 3 or fewer: second reward each, no card; exactly two tied first in 4P: others compete for third, nobody takes card. Combat rewards: 0 strength gets none.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward allowing 3 spice for 1 VP, a doubled reward permits paying 3 spice twice for 2 VP, or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more sandworms “double”; location control and battle icons cannot; optional cost may be paid a second time, example 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: Check after winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply. Match against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match must be flipped face down for 1 VP. During Endgame the wild icon may match any one of the three icons, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: after win, match card with another “face-up Conflict or Objective”; “must” flip pair; Endgame wild matches any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence you gain 1 VP and lose that reward below 2, regaining it on reaching 2 again. At 4 you gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; first to 4 gains Alliance token and 1 VP, which follows token ownership. Merely tying the holder does not steal it: a challenger must rise above. FAQ adds transfer when holder loses Influence after being tied.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 VP reverses below 2; separate 4 rewards have stated reversal rules; tying does not steal Alliance, rising above transfers. FAQ transfer trigger on holder losing Influence after tie.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled to buy one card or split across cards. The Row refills to five immediately, so you may buy a replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: spend during Reveal before/between/after effects; pool or split; Row always five; acquired card face up in discard.

answers.answer: At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space gets 1 bonus spice added to any already there; visiting harvests all bonus spice. Worm summoning is blocked at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery and Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; removing it permits worms at any Conflict. Hooks are normally required only where the effect specifies them, are retained rather than spent, and a worm is placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers; Sandworms: Hooks requirement is effect-specific and not universal; protected Conflict spaces; worms directly deployed and never garrisoned; hooks never spent.

answers.answer: The threshold or empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame at Recall, at the end of the round. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall: check 10+ VP or empty deck; Scoring: Endgame Intrigue first, then most VP; tiebreak sequence listed.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with 2 of the 20 standard contracts face up and 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards. Shaddam is an optional Leader. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay out of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: flip two of 20 face up, remaining 18 face down; shuffle 4 additional cards of each deck; Shaddam “not required.” Contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix set, leave in box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM the contract icon takes one of two face-up contracts and replaces it with a face-up bank contract; if all contracts have been taken, it instead gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the shown spice total that turn; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts: take and replace; if all taken icon gives 2 Solari. Completing contracts lists Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow conditions.

answers.answer: No: a space contract gained after you already sent an Agent there this turn waits until a future turn; you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must have held contract when Agent sent; then “announce it, gain the rewards it shows,” flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives go randomly to the humans, and the First Player marker determines which human starts. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; human First Player alternates between humans. Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup: one Rival, objectives and human first player; turn order stated; Agents: Rival never takes Reveal.

answers.answer: Ignore an occupied Hagal destination and reveal another card. A Place Spy card only attempts to place at an empty specified-type post; whether it succeeds or fails, immediately reveal another card and continue this Agent turn. Rivals ignore ordinary space costs/effects and use only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied destination ignored/reveal again; Place Spy does not place Agent and immediately reveal another; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle immediately.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing those whose 1–3P/4/6P marks do not fit the player count, then distribute one eligible Objective face up to each player; the First Player marker shown selects First Player. Shaddam may not be selected without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; omit mismatched Objectives, shuffle and deal face up; marked Objective determines First Player.

answers.answer: The bank’s Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if they run out. By contrast, an empty personal troop supply prevents recruiting more until troops return there. Gains come from the bank and payments return there.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources and worms “not meant to be limited”; troop recruitment restriction; gain resources from bank and payments return to bank.

answers.answer: Phases: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict first, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise and begin next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure gives five phases in order; Phase 1 reveals Conflict then each draws five; Phase 5 recalls Agents, passes marker and begins again if no win.

answers.answer: Yes: space, Agent-box and Influence effects may be carried out in any order. No: entry costs and requirements must be paid/met before effects, so this visit’s Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: “all these effects in any order”; requirements/costs before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid and gained once per turn; the exception is sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory, with “may,” optional arrow costs and black-X trash exceptions; direct self-trash is mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs: once per turn except doubling. FAQ Mandatory effects and costs lists optional/mandatory cases and Intrigue costs.

answers.answer: Normally place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post connected as specified by the effect. If supply is empty, you may recall one of your Spies for no effect first. If the effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, that type must be connected or placement is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy icon allows post placement, if none in supply may first recall for no effect; specific icon-type requirement can prohibit placement.

answers.answer: No. Infiltrate bypasses another player’s Agent, not your own. A Spy cannot be used without a card to send an Agent: recalling for Spy effects still requires a played card and does not waive costs or requirements. You cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies says Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent and Gather Intelligence is an effect after sending Agent. FAQ Spies says card still required; no two Gather Intelligence recalls on one placement.

answers.answer: Whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent to a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, its controller gets 1 Solari; at controlled Imperial Basin the controller gets 1 spice. A player who wins the location Conflict places a Control marker, replacing any opponent’s marker. When that Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: visitor bonuses listed, markers replace opponent; controller gets defensive troop from supply when relevant Conflict revealed, without Agent visit.

answers.answer: In three-player play, a second-place tie gives each tied player the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and Conflict card and there are no further rewards. A third-place tie gets nothing. A three-player first-place tie means each gets second reward, no other rewards, and nobody takes card.
answers.evidence: Combat tie table: second tie and third tie outcomes; first tie with 3 or fewer gets second each, no card.

answers.answer: In a normal three-player Conflict, first and second get their rewards; untied third gets nothing. The third reward is used only for a second-place tie. In two-player play with Rival, the same 2–3 player reward rules apply.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive reward, third nothing; printed third used for tie second; Rival counts as competitor.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only in Combat; Endgame Intrigue at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from deck, and reveal only when played; after resolving, ordinary played Intrigues go face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If Intrigue deck empties, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Player Turns / Intrigue cards: timing categories, hold face down, reveal on play and discard after resolving. FAQ Draw timing: exhausted deck discard reshuffled.

answers.answer: No; ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon chooses one Intrigue from your hand. Secrets steals one at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand, not Intrigue unless specified. Trashing: separate Intrigue icon. Board space table Secrets and steal icon: random one from each 4+ opponent.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile or in play; return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or card instructs itself to be trashed. The Spice Must Flow VP gained on acquisition remains if later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; FAQ Victory says Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained if trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment you acquire the card. If your deck is empty when you need a draw, reshuffle discard into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost after Reveal and cannot be carried over.
answers.evidence: FAQ Acquire box timing; Acquiring Cards explains reshuffle when unable to draw and unused Persuasion is lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed at Reveal remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed. Other Fremen cards in play enable Fremen Bond; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen card, mutual activation regardless of order, cards remain until Clean Up.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents, not the one just sent; it may be reused on another Agent turn that round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison; “retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon: “other” Agent, usable again same round; Retreat definition and FAQ allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence must put both with one chosen Faction; it cannot split. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; minimum-Influence effects require the stated Influence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two Factions; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the formerly tied opponents are eligible and the former holder chooses which receives the Alliance. If holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; old holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring and FAQ—Alliance loss: if several were tied former holder chooses; if holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody 4+, return token; loses VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that point, is used then, and discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing states all three distinctions.

answers.answer: No: a “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: cannot play after tie; if received as winning reward it can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory explicitly states both.

answers.answer: No: contracts for a space must be fulfilled together by one Agent placement, so you cannot delay them separately after visiting. Contract is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but must have been held when Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all held contracts for same space with one placement; another effect in any order; must hold it when sending.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts; they do not start in anyone’s possession. His Sardaukar Commander permits choosing one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring. His Signet Ring deployment restriction takes effect immediately upon playing Signet Ring to send an Agent, and lasts that turn only.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Shaddam: set-aside contract option when acquiring, not initially possessed; restriction immediately upon Signet Ring and only for that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica starts with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications and FAQ Reverend Mother Jessica statement.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; it can happen again later after losing Influence and regaining it, but descending through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Margot/Irulan; Spacing Guild’s Favor clarification.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is Spice Trade: draw a card and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise gain 2 Solari (also if none remain); it is not a Faction, so no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service is Emperor: gain 1 Emperor Influence and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari (also if none remain). It does advance Emperor Influence as an explicit effect.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table entries and explanatory note: Accept Contract and Dutiful Service effects; Spice Trade/Landsraad are not Factions, while Dutiful Service has explicit Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, not Combat; gain one Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one sandworm. Both harvest all bonus spice regardless of choice; Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Maker entries say bonus spice plus options; Sandworms says Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if lacking, recruit one troop and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall; it gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr entry states requirements and two choices.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari each visit and is not Combat. First visit puts Councilor on an unoccupied seat and provides 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for rest of game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 afterward; each player may gain it once per game. The third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival’s Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row; notes Rival gain also lowers human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad icon, requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Effects: may discard an Intrigue to draw one, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. No automatic Emperor Influence is listed.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; explanatory rule says Landsraad is not a Faction and only explicit Influence counts.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Guild Influence and costs 3 spice; it gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction. The free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, Combat status not marked (so no normal deployment); choose 0 or 2 Solari, recruit two troops, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat; choose 0 or 1 spice, gain respectively 2 or 4 Solari; its controller gets 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery entries; guide says only marked Combat spaces permit deployment.

answers.answer: Heighliner costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is Combat. Desert Tactics costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card; Combat. Sardaukar costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; it is not marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries identify costs, effects and Combat markings.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost, draw Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, gains 1 BG Influence, draws a card and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost, gains 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None are marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries; Faction icon identifies access; only Combat-marked spaces allow deployment.

answers.answer: False Orders: affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders and Litany Against Fear bullets.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card Manipulate removed. You may acquire it by another means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate bullet.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at track bottoms, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside board, three Spies and 1 water; score/Combat marker are 0. Shuffle House Hagal near Rival and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. Rival’s 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup; Rival can win and 10+ triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as its combined Solari, spice, Intrigues and water reach its printed Swordmaster value, spend that amount; count each unit/card as one. Spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigues, water; keep leftovers. Its third Agent is usable that current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster paragraph.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it separately spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed seven-resource total does not qualify.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: “whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.”

answers.answer: Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains/losses 2-Influence VP and Alliance VP like a human, but gets no resource bonus at 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat/Influence paragraphs; numbered Influence meaning in Rival Agent-turn rules.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, select only the destination matching current conditions—Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If that selected destination is occupied, reveal a new card rather than use the other.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns two-destination card rule.

answers.answer: Yes: at every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if it recruited none. At a noncombat space recruited troops go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent placement; only the bonus is missed.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: at Combat deploy up to two even no recruit; non-Combat garrison. Conditional bonus absence never prevents placing.

answers.answer: Unless specified, Rival places Spy at first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. It never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes paragraph.

answers.answer: Scheme-recruited troops before placement also deploy if the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, then Rival immediately reveals another Hagal card because it sent no Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes scheme timing; Rival Agent turns Place Spy sequence.

answers.answer: Rival collects all bonus spice at the Maker space. At Hagga/Deep Desert with Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one/two worms instead of base spice; if it summons none, it takes base 2/4 spice. Without Hooks it cannot take worm option and takes base spice. Protected Conflict prevents summoning, so it takes base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces paragraph; it always collects all bonus spice, worm choices with Hooks and permitted Conflict, base spice if none summoned.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. Unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes, Rival gains control bonuses on visits, defensive troop on Conflict reveal, battle-icon VP, and doubles rewards when it has a sandworm. It takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: During Reveal resolution, total and announce strength and set Combat marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving, including when later effects change it. Above 20, flip marker to +20 side and start again from beginning of track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn says strength announced/set at any point while resolving, update as needed; Strength explains +20 marker.

answers.answer: Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not merely when revealing it. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one Spy from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. By itself it is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate no-card recall options with their own conditions/effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Recall Spy definition, then separate Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; Discarding rule.

answers.answer: With a sandworm doubling a reward granting one free-choice Influence, the reward is gained twice and the choices may be the same or different Factions. A single effect granting two Influence with free choice requires choosing one Faction for both, not splitting.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling gives example doubled 2 Influence with same or different Factions; Influence rule says gain two can’t choose two different Factions.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival’s printed Signet Ring ability from its Rival card when Hagal shows that effect. The human’s Signet Ring card and Reveal turn are not needed.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: “follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities”; Agent turns include Signet Ring among Hagal effects; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks takes a token if Rival lacks one and does nothing if it already has one. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if Wall already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit icon, costs nothing, and is not Combat. Gain 1 BG Influence and draw an Intrigue from deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade icon, no entry cost, and is Combat. Visitor gets 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice. Controller gets 1 spice; if same player controls it, that player gets both amounts.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; controlled location effects resolve for visitor and controller even same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Players draw five cards after that reveal.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Conflict placed “on top of any Conflict cards remaining”; then each draws five.

answers.answer: Each human’s four Influence cubes start on the bottom spaces of the four Faction tracks. Alliance tokens begin on their four marked Faction track areas, so no human begins holding one. Shield Wall token starts on marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks, cubes at bottom, Shield Wall below Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: In 3–4-player play, First Player takes first turn and play continues clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped for rest of phase; phase ends after all players have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, priority begins with First Player and proceeds clockwise; an eligible player may play any number then pass.
answers.evidence: Player Turns paragraph; Combat Intrigue paragraph.

answers.answer: Reveal turn steps are: reveal remaining hand; resolve Reveal effects; Clean Up. Effects may be resolved in any order, and Persuasion can be spent before, between or after effects.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn steps state this exact order and effects “in any order.”

answers.answer: Without CHOAM, shuffle each human’s 10-card starting deck face down; shuffle Intrigue deck face down; omit CHOAM cards, shuffle Imperium deck face down and deal five face-up cards into Row; place Prepare the Way and Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies in supply; Councilor token in supply; three Control markers in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6 plus Initial card states table.

answers.answer: Ordinarily acquire any of five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Cost is top right. These ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes, ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even if legal. Shield Wall detonation says you may remove it; once removed it is gone for rest of game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts says ordinary icons optional; Shield Wall says “may remove” and cannot return.

answers.answer: The played card must have a matching normal Agent icon for the destination, or its Spy Agent icon with a Spy at a connected post. A Spy connected to Shipping alone does not make a City-only card legal there. If card has Spy Agent icon, connected Spy enables sending there without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn states matching icon requirement and connected Spy alone insufficient; Special Rules explains Spy Agent icon.

answers.answer: Yes: play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; resources it grants before entry join available supply and can pay. Resources from the Agent card or destination are gained after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: pre-placement Plot gains can pay; post-placement destination/card gains cannot pay entry.

answers.answer: No. After humans Reveal, skip them and continue Rival Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply; proceed to Combat only after both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule.

answers.answer: Standard 2–4p board-space reference (icon; Combat?): Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, no; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table, listing all 22 spaces with Agent icon and Combat markings.

answers.answer: When the relevant Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict; no Agent visit is needed. After rewards all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus timing and Critical Locations paragraph; Resolve Combat cleanup says markers reset to 0; Makers follows Combat.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you; send one Agent from your Leader to an eligible unoccupied board space; use that card’s Agent box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile, or move an Agent already on board as your placement; the Agent must be sent from Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one hand card, send Agent from Leader; use Agent box. Recall/board rules treat board Agent as already placed; used cards are in play until Clean Up.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent, so resolving board-space effects first cannot postpone it.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send Agent; ordering effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no worms, first, second and third receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth gets none. Highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player ordinary first/second/third paid; winner has highest strength and takes card.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select at random.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3: take a Leader “choose, or select at random.”

answers.answer: Ordinary draw effects draw from your own deck; you cannot choose directly from discard. If deck is empty when drawing, shuffle discard into a new deck and continue.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing/ordinary draw bullet.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place deck near shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A later acquired token moves from bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: all 4 Hooks in common bank, none to human; acquired token moves onto garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise strength, adjust marker when that card resolves during Combat Intrigue window; Reveal strength is not fixed. Use adjusted strength shown on track to resolve Combat.
answers.evidence: Combat: adjust marker when card resolves; Reveal total not fixed; resolve using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice and water come from the bank, not another player’s supply. Payments return to bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: whenever gain resources take from bank; whenever pay return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contracts face down first, then flip two face up onto marked board spaces; remaining 18 stay face down in bank. The offers are random; players do not choose them or preset the bank order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: “Shuffle the 20 contracts face down, then flip two face up”; remaining 18 face down in bank.
